src/domain/order/Order.ts: Order.place calls OrderLine.consolidate(lines), so the line-merging rule stays in OrderLine.ts
src/domain/order/OrderStatus.ts: FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE, nextStatus, isCancellable and parseOrderStatus put all status rules in a single file
src/domain/order/OrderLine.ts: OrderLine.of validates productId and quantity, and consolidate only combines lines that are already valid
src/domain/order/OrderRepository.ts: the interface's findById, findByStatus(status: OrderStatus) and save(order: Order) are written against the module's own types
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is cohesive. It covers one concern, the order aggregate, through four files: the aggregate root (Order), a value object (OrderLine), the persistence port (OrderRepository) and the lifecycle rules (OrderStatus). Each rule has one home. OrderStatus.ts owns the order statuses move through and which statuses can be cancelled. Order.ts calls nextStatus and isCancellable rather than encoding transitions itself. OrderLine.ts owns line validation and merging lines for the same product, and Order.place calls OrderLine.consolidate rather than merging inline. OrderRepository uses the module's own types (Order, OrderStatus). One minor point: CANCELLABLE hard-codes ['placed','paid','packed'] instead of deriving 'before shipped' from FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE. Both lists sit in the same file next to each other, so this is not duplication across the module. OrderLine.consolidate calls the private constructor directly, which skips the validation in `of`. That is safe because its inputs are already-validated OrderLines and the sums of positive integers stay positive, so the module's abstraction is not bypassed.
